title: Select the next task requiring processing
objective: Add sdlc task next --work-item <work-item> as a deterministic read-only command that returns the first task whose processingStatus is unprocessed.

branch.name: main
branch.rationale: The repository is already on the main branch and the user requested preparation, processing, and per-task commits on the current repository.

request.text:
prepare a new work item for 'sdlc task next --work-item <work-item> that pulls the next task that requires processing. commit the new work item.

Process the new work item, commit per task.

scope.name: next-task-command
scope.description: Add sdlc task next --work-item <work-item> to select the next task requiring host processing.
scope.reason: Operators need a deterministic command that identifies the next unprocessed task without scanning task records manually.

scope.name: processing-status-selection
scope.description: Select only tasks with processingStatus unprocessed, preserving deterministic task-file ordering and leaving task files unchanged.
scope.reason: processingStatus is the authoritative host-processing boundary in the task envelope.

scope.name: next-task-response
scope.description: Persist a closed response schema for selected-task and no-next-task results, including the selected task summary when available.
scope.reason: CLI JSON response objects require durable versioned schemas.

nonGoals.name: task-processing
nonGoals.description: Do not mutate processingStatus, execute a task, lock a task, or transition task/work-item lifecycle state.
nonGoals.reason: The command selects work; a separate processor owns execution and lifecycle mutation.

nonGoals.name: task-ordering-change
nonGoals.description: Do not change task discovery ordering, task envelope parsing, task-list output, or invalid work-item option behavior.
nonGoals.reason: task next reuses the established deterministic task discovery boundary.

nonGoals.name: provider-and-production-runtime
nonGoals.description: Do not add provider calls, HTTP services, persistence, deployment, or production release behavior.
nonGoals.reason: WI-0009 is limited to local task selection and response serialization.

items.name: next-task-selection
items.description: sdlc task next --work-item <work-item> must select the first discovered task whose processingStatus is unprocessed.
items.reason: The command must identify the next task requiring host processing without changing task state.

acceptanceCriteria.description: For a work item with unprocessed tasks, the command returns zero and selects the first unprocessed task in the existing deterministic task order.
Tasks with processingStatus processing_in_progress, processing_completed, processing_blocked, or processing_failed are not selected.

items.name: next-task-response
items.description: The command must provide stable human-readable and JSON results for a selected task and for the no-next-task case.
items.reason: Interactive and automated callers need to distinguish a selected task from an exhausted work item.

acceptanceCriteria.description: The persisted response schema covers selected and no-next-task results and includes the work-item ID, selection status, and selected task summary when present.
When no task requires processing, the command returns a stable zero-exit response indicating no next task rather than an error.

items.name: selector-and-read-only-boundary
items.description: The command must require --work-item <work-item>, reject missing/duplicate/invalid/unknown selectors consistently, and not modify task files.
items.reason: Selection must remain scoped and safe to call repeatedly before a processor executes the task.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Focused tests cover valid selection, no-next-task behavior, missing/duplicate/invalid/unknown selectors, and unchanged task-file bytes.

items.name: task-next-validation
items.description: The implementation and validation evidence must cover existing WI-0008 task states and a deterministic temporary fixture with mixed processing statuses.
items.reason: The current repository mostly contains completed tasks, so selection and no-next-task behavior both require explicit evidence.

acceptanceCriteria.description: yarn test and fresh-process task next checks pass for selected, exhausted, and invalid-input cases.
